messages.author: 41bda30b9abcf1fd
messages.subject: ""independent pathways" model
parts:
Hello.
I am working with a commonfactor model with 3 phenotypes – ph1, ph2 and ph3. I am using the userGWAS function to avoid problems with negative residual variance for the phenotype ph1.
The model:
model <- “F1 =~ph1+ph2+ph3
F1~SNP
ph1~~a*ph1
a >.001”

Usermodel <- userGWAS(covstruc = input1, SNPs=input2, estimation =”ML”, model=model, modelchi=T, GC=”none”, sub=c(“F1~SNP”), printwarn=T)

I now want to obtain heterogeneity (Q) index as described in the tutorial “Optional step 5: Run a follow-up model to obtain heterogeneity (Q) index)”. I have defined the following “independent pathways” model:

model <- ”F1 =~ph1+ph2+ph3
ph1+ph2+ph3~SNP
ph1~~a*ph1
a>.001”

Usermodel <- userGWAS(covstruc=input1, SNPs = input2, estimation = “ML”, model=model, modelchi = T, GC = “none”, sub = c(“ph1+ph2+ph3~SNP”), printwarn = T)

When I run the “independent pathways” model above, I receive an empty table as result. I am not sure, if it is the model, that is defined incorrectly or if it is the wrong component of the model (sub=(“ph1+ph2+ph3~SNP”)), I request. Can you help me with this issue?

Thank you, Trine

messages.subject: Re: ""independent pathways" model
parts:
Cant say fr certain but could be the sub= argument doesnt parse regresisons with multiple left hand side's.

could try something like:

model <- ”F1 =~ph1+ph2+ph3
ph1~SNP

ph2~SNP

ph3~SNP


ph1~~a*ph1
a>.001”

Usermodel <- userGWAS(covstruc=input1, SNPs = input2, estimation = “ML”, model=model, modelchi = T, GC = “none”, sub = c(“ph1~SNP","ph2~SNP","ph3~SNP”), printwarn = T)
